summary: Deadwood Lookout, a CCC-built L-4 cab on Idaho's Boise National Forest staffed into the early 1970s, was restored over ten years and is now a popular Forest Service rental.

access.note: Forest Service rental via Recreation.gov; narrow, steep, winding access road.

visit.trail_note: High-clearance vehicle recommended for the dirt access road.

events.note: Earliest known structure: a log crib platform.
12x12-foot frame cabin with cupola replaced the log crib platform.
Current ground-mounted L-4 cab built by the CCC, per Recreation.gov and Firelookout.com.
National Historic Lookout Register instead gives 1936 for the current structure, replacing the 1924 cupola cabin.
Lookout Jay Broadie recorded staffing the tower.
Recreation.gov: actively used as a fire lookout until 1972.
Idaho Fire Lookouts instead gives 1973 as when the tower went to emergency status.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, May 12, 2003, after a ten-year restoration.

evidence.supports: 1916 log crib platform as earliest structure
1924 cupola cabin, 1934 L-4 cab, use into 1970s emergencies
evidence.quote: Developed in 1916 with a log crib platform, a 12x12' frame cabin with cupola replaced it in 1924. In 1934, this ground-mounted L-4 cab was built. It was used for emergencies in the 1970's

evidence.supports: 1936 build date, replaced 1924 cupola, CCC structure, restoration, standby status
evidence.quote: Deadwood Lookout on the Boise National Forest looks much as it did the day it went into service in 1936, replacing a cupola lookout built in 1924. This CCC structure was active for many years but is now on standby status

evidence.supports: 1934 CCC build, staffed until 1972, access road, rental popularity
evidence.quote: the current one was built in 1934 by the Civilian Conservation Corps. It was actively used as a fire lookout until 1972.
high clearance vehicles are recommended for the dirt access road because it is narrow, steep and winding... peak season is late June through mid-October

evidence.supports: Jay Broadie 1953, 1973 emergency status, 2003 NHLR registration
evidence.quote:
1973 – Went to emergency status
2003 – Added to The National Historic Lookout Register
Hanes A "Jay" Broadie (Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry)

resolved_conflicts.field: build year of current L-4 cab
resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1936 for the current structure; Recreation.gov and Firelookout.com independently agree on 1934. Reported both, noting NHLR as the outlier against two agreeing sources.
The brief's queue data already flagged a lat/lon mismatch between NHLR and RIDB coordinates; not independently re-verified within this research pass.

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict (1934 vs 1936) left unresolved per two-against-one source split. No structure height (as opposed to elevation) was found in sources, so height_m was omitted.
